title: Kim Hak-sun's public testimony
summary: On 14 August 1991, at a news conference in Seoul, Kim Hak-sun, then 67, said publicly that she had been a sex slave for the Imperial Japanese Army during the Second World War. She was the first woman in South Korea to break her silence, and her demand for historical truth drew responses from other victims at home and abroad.

uncertainty.note: Exact day given by the Korea Herald and the Korea Times; Amnesty gives August 1991.

importance.justification: The first public testimony by a surviving former comfort woman in South Korea; it opened a wider movement for redress.

audience_note: Concerns wartime sexual slavery; the record states it in general terms without detail.
